title: Why Clean Dryer Vents? Fire Risk & Airflow
headline: Lint past the trap is a fire problem — NFPA numbers, CPSC notes, and when to book
description: Why clean dryer vents? Lint, fire risk (NFPA), longer dry times — and how professional cleaning helps homes.

sections.heading: The lint your trap misses ends up in the vent
paragraphs: Most homeowners empty the lint trap after every load — but the trap only catches part of what drying produces. The rest travels into the exhaust duct, where it packs over months and years.

[CPSC staff work on electric dryers](https://www.cpsc.gov/s3fs-public/pdfs/blk_pdf_electric.pdf) found lint can accumulate in the appliance even when the dryer is installed correctly, properly vented, and the lint screen is cleaned between cycles. That is why cleaning the **vent duct** — not only the trap — matters for fire safety and dryer performance.

sections.heading: How dryer fires start — and how common they are
paragraphs: According to the [National Fire Protection Association analysis of home dryer fires for 2014–2018](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/research/nfpa-research/fire-statistical-reports/home-fires-involving-clothes-dryers-and-washing-machines), U.S. fire departments responded to an estimated average of about **13,820 home dryer fires per year**. Those fires caused an average of about seven civilian deaths, 344 civilian injuries, and $233 million in direct property damage annually.

**Failure to clean** was a factor in about **32%** of those fires, and **dust, fiber, or lint** was the item first ignited in about **27%**. (Older [USFA topical reporting](https://www.usfa.fema.gov/downloads/pdf/statistics/v13i7.pdf) used a narrower scope; NFPA remains the clearest public source for the failure-to-clean share.)

As lint packs the vent, airflow drops and exhaust backs up. The dryer runs hotter and longer. Trapped heat plus flammable lint is a preventable recipe for ignition — which is why full-length vent cleaning is one of the highest-ROI home maintenance visits we sell.
listItems: ~13,820 home dryer fires/year (NFPA 2014–2018)
Failure to clean ~32%; lint first ignited ~27%
Average ~7 deaths, 344 injuries, $233M damage/year

sections.heading: 5 signs your dryer vent is overdue
paragraphs: Do not wait for a fire to discover a packed vent:
listItems: Clothes take more than one cycle to dry
The dryer or laundry room feels unusually hot mid-cycle
A burning smell during operation — stop the dryer and call a pro
Lint around the exterior vent flap or behind the dryer
Exterior damper that barely opens or stays shut while the dryer runs

sections.heading: Homes that pack lint faster
paragraphs: Some layouts and habits shorten the safe interval between cleanings:
listItems: High laundry volume — multiple loads daily; consider cleaning every six months
Long or winding runs — more elbows mean more places lint packs; long vertical condo risers are classic
Flexible plastic ducting — traps lint more easily than rigid metal; upgrade when possible
Pets — fine fur passes the trap and accelerates blockage
Skipped lint-trap cleaning — missing loads sends more lint into the duct

sections.heading: What professional vent cleaning actually protects
paragraphs: Clearing the full run is fire prevention first — and dryer performance second:
listItems: Fire risk reduction — removing compacted lint addresses a leading, preventable factor in dryer fires (NFPA: failure to clean)
Faster drying — a clear vent lets moisture escape so more loads finish in one cycle
Less heat stress on the appliance — restricted exhaust makes dryers run hotter and longer
Safer exhaust for gas dryers — blocked vents can interfere with proper exhaust of combustion products; keep the path clear and fuel-burning equipment serviced
Documented close-out — we verify airflow and the exterior damper before we leave

sections.heading: Why a hardware-store brush kit usually is not enough
paragraphs: A basic kit can clear lint near the dryer connection. Compacted buildup 10–30 feet down — especially around elbows — often stays put. DIY also risks disconnecting joints in a chase or attic.
Professional service uses rotary brushes for the full length, industrial vacuum containment, inspection for crushed or unsafe duct, and airflow verification at the end.
listItems: High-powered rotary brushes for the full duct length
Industrial vacuums that capture dislodged lint
Inspection for crushed, disconnected, or unsafe sections
Airflow check before reconnecting the dryer

sections.heading: What happens on our dryer vent visit
paragraphs: Typical sequence when Amazon Air Duct Cleaning services a dryer vent:
listItems: Route assessment — dryer to exterior cap; note length, elbows, material
Dryer disconnect and area prep
Full-length brush cleaning
Industrial vacuuming of dislodged lint
Exterior damper and cap check
Airflow verification before reconnect

sections.heading: Habits between annual cleanings
paragraphs: Most homes benefit from professional cleaning about once a year. Between visits:
listItems: Clean the lint trap before every load
Check the exterior vent monthly — damper free, no nests or debris
Do not overload the dryer
Prefer rigid metal ducting over plastic flex hose
Do not run the dryer while asleep or away from home

sections.heading: A clear vent is cheap insurance — book it
paragraphs: Dryer fires remain common, and many are tied to failure to clean. NFPA’s 2014–2018 numbers — roughly 13,820 fires a year, failure to clean in about a third — are why a packed vent is worth fixing before the dryer overheats.

faq.q: How often should dryer vents be cleaned?
faq.a: About once a year for most homes. High laundry volume, long vent runs, or pets may need service every six months.

faq.q: Does cleaning a dryer vent eliminate fire risk?
faq.a: No cleaning guarantees zero risk. Clearing lint from the full duct addresses a leading, preventable factor in dryer fires (NFPA: failure to clean).

faq.q: Can I clean the vent myself with a brush kit?
faq.a: DIY kits help near the opening but often miss compacted lint deeper in long or winding runs. Pros brush and vacuum the full length and verify airflow.
